summary: Read-only review complete. Revision 8 addresses the three prior findings; four material gaps remain. No edits, builds, tests, network access, or .env reads performed.

findings.title: Native login can issue a session using a superseded second factor
findings.detail: routes/admin.ts verifies the second factor before calling createAdminSessionIfCredential. auth/admin-session.ts:79-87 rechecks only the password hash and whether a factor was verified, not which factor or epoch. Pause login after verification, disable and re-enable TOTP, then resume: the password hash is unchanged and secondFactorVerified remains true, so login creates a session after the factor change and its session revocation. The native step-up correction does not cover this issuance path.
findings.fix:
| Admin password change (`admin-session.ts`) | `admin_user` `FOR UPDATE` → kept session `FOR UPDATE` | unchanged; trigger clears step-ups |
| Native admin login (`routes/admin.ts` → `createAdminSessionIfCredential`) | password/factor verification outside the transaction → admin `FOR SHARE` → password-hash check and boolean factor check → session insert | **restructured**: `findAdminByEmail` reads `security_epoch`, `password_hash` and the stored TOTP version together before password/factor verification. Carry that snapshot through login and require its epoch and stored TOTP version to equal the locked owner row before inserting the session; also retain the password-hash equality check, using the replacement hash only when this request's conditional rehash succeeded. Reject a changed snapshot with the generic login failure. A boolean `secondFactorVerified` alone is insufficient. Add deterministic real-route tests pausing login after successful factor verification, disabling and re-enabling TOTP with both the same and a different secret, then resuming login and proving that no session is created. |

findings.title: Bulk session revocation can deadlock with passkey deletion and trigger invalidation
findings.detail: The new discipline locks the calling session before updating all sessions during passkey deletion. The trigger also updates multiple sessions. Meanwhile, admin-settings-advanced.ts:656 and revokeAllSessionsForAdmin delete sessions without locking the owner. With sessions A and B, passkey deletion can hold B while revocation deletes A and waits for B; deletion then waits for A while clearing step-ups. The owner lock cannot serialize a revocation that never acquires it.
findings.fix: | Session revocations (staff management, agent lifecycle, logout) | Human bulk revocation deletes sessions without an owner lock; agent lifecycle also holds grant/token locks | **restructured**: every human multi-session revocation takes the target `admin_user` row `FOR UPDATE` before locking or deleting any session rows. Apply this to the direct staff revoke-sessions transaction in `admin-settings-advanced.ts`, `revokeAllSessionsForAdmin` and `revokeOtherAdminSessions`; preserve the existing authorization checks and atomic audit. Password and factor mutations already hold this owner lock. Single-session logout and agent-only lifecycle operations remain unchanged. Session-bound artifacts are orphaned and expire. Add deterministic real-route races with at least two live sessions between bulk revocation and passkey deletion, password change and TOTP-triggered invalidation, covering the interleaving where revocation would otherwise lock a different session before reaching the calling session; require completion without deadlock retries. |

findings.title: The TOTP replay guard retains an owner/advisory lock inversion
findings.detail: second-factor.ts:84 acquires the totp-step advisory lock before inserting admin_totp_used_step at line 89. That insert takes an implicit FK KEY SHARE lock on admin_user. Conversely, mutateAdminSecondFactor locks admin_user FOR UPDATE at admin-staff.ts:72, then calls verifySecondFactorTx at line 100 and waits for the same advisory lock. Native step-up, login, or recovery-code regeneration can therefore hold the advisory lock while waiting for the owner, as disable holds the owner while waiting for the advisory lock. The revised native step-up row retains this verification path.
findings.fix: | Admin factor mutations and standalone TOTP verification (`admin-staff.ts`, `second-factor.ts`) | Factor mutation: credential advisory → admin `FOR UPDATE` → session `FOR UPDATE` → replay advisory; standalone TOTP verification: replay advisory → replay-row insert → implicit admin FK `KEY SHARE` | **restructured**: standalone `verifyTotpOnce` acquires the existing admin row `FOR SHARE` in its own transaction before acquiring the `totp-step` advisory lock or touching replay rows, and refuses a missing owner. Transactional factor verification continues to use the caller's already-held admin `FOR UPDATE` lock before the replay advisory lock; never acquire the owner after the replay advisory lock. Keep standalone verification committed before the later native step-up mutation transaction, including its captured-epoch and credential-snapshot checks. Add the TOTP invariant check (passkeys exist → 409 `PASSKEYS_ENROLLED` on disable); the trigger performs epoch/step-up invalidation. Add deterministic real-route races between TOTP disable and standalone TOTP verification through login, native step-up, enrolment and recovery-code regeneration, covering both lock interleavings without retries or sleeps. |

findings.title: Mailbox-derived grants survive the end of bootstrap eligibility
findings.detail: Deleting unconsumed mailbox tokens does not invalidate grants already minted by branch D or registration challenges already minted from those grants by branch E. First registration changes neither the owner epoch nor the session. Consequently, a second pre-issued mailbox grant or registration challenge still passes the documented checks after a passkey exists, permitting another enrollment without proving that passkey. Checking eligibility only at mailbox confirmation leaves this derived-authorization path open.
findings.fix: | Customer passkey registered (new image) | n/a | n/a | n/a | + row | del all unconsumed M; when registration changes the owner from zero to one current-epoch credential, also delete all of that customer's P/G in the same owner-locked transaction, including outstanding registration challenges and previously confirmed mailbox grants. This ends every pending bootstrap authorization without invalidating the newly inserted credential or changing the owner epoch. Test two mailbox grants confirmed before first registration, with one already exchanged for a registration challenge: after first registration commits, neither the remaining grant nor the outstanding challenge may authorize another enrollment or deletion. | n/a |
